metadata.description: The portable OS-patching process: the definition every engine shares. It names no engine; it is what policy gates, schedules reference and compliance reports against, and what a provider must satisfy to declare `execute_workflows / Automation.OSPatch`.

inputs_schema.description: The typed parameters a run accepts, as a JSON Schema.

outputs_schema.description: The typed results a run publishes; every engine must satisfy it.

idempotency.description: Re-run semantics, a bounded codelist: idempotent, at_most_once, at_least_once.

retry_policy.description: How a failed run retries: attempts and backoff.

compensation.description: What undo means, if anything, a bounded codelist. Rollback is a different process type, declared as such.

affected_entities.description: Which records a run may mutate: the blast-radius declaration, as references.

targets.description: The hosts to patch: references to Machine records or to a grouping.

patch_policy.description: What to patch, a bounded codelist: security, all, kernel.

reboot_policy.description: Reboot behaviour, a bounded codelist: never, if-required (may name a maintenance window), always.

exclusions.description: Packages held back as known fragile.

last_run_status.description: Outcome of the most recent patch run (succeeded | failed | partial) — the readiness signal schedules and compliance reports consume.

last_run_timestamp.description: RFC 3339 UTC instant of the most recent run completion.

packages_updated.description: Count of packages changed in the most recent run — the drift-facing magnitude signal.

context.purpose: The portable OS-patching process — what org policy gates, schedules reference, and compliance reports against, independent of which engine executes it.
context.plain_description: Declares that hosts get patched: which package sets, within which maintenance windows, at which severity floor. Both engines (blue today, green tomorrow) satisfy this one definition — swapping engines never touches the declared process.
use_when: You schedule or gate OS patching as governed automation
You need engine-portable patch compliance reporting
